run.procedureSummary:
Each cycle runs five moves in order. Each move is finished across all six crucibles before the next one starts.
1. Charge: add that cycle's charge row to crucibles 1-6. No volume check at this step.
2. Overflow: walk crucibles 1 to 6. Any melt over a crucible's working volume (10,8,12,6,9,7) is moved into the next crucible before that one is judged, so overflow can chain. Overflow off crucible 6 goes to slag.
3. Temperature, on the post-overflow quantities: a BASE crucible at or above its upper mark (7,6,9,5,7,5) becomes SUPERHEATED. A SUPERHEATED crucible at or below its lower mark (3,2,4,2,3,2) becomes BASE. Anything else holds. Every change is logged.
4. Bleed: read all six quantities and states first, then apply every transfer from that reading. A BASE crucible skims floor(q/4) to slag. A SUPERHEATED crucible sends floor(q/2) to the crucible before it (crucible 1's half goes to slag). A crucible may end over volume; it is not corrected until the next cycle's overflow.
5. Emergency tap: total the line. If the total is strictly over 38, each crucible loses floor(q/2) to slag and keeps q - floor(q/2), and the cycle is logged.
Slag tally = overflow off 6 + BASE skims + crucible 1's superheated half + tap removals.

openPoints.point: How to round when halving in the emergency tap
openPoints.assumption: 'Any split rounds down' is applied to the amount removed: floor(q/2) goes to slag and the crucible keeps q - floor(q/2), so an odd crucible keeps the larger half. This matches how I rounded the bleed, where the amount moved is rounded down.

openPoints.point: How to round the bleed amounts
openPoints.assumption: BASE skim = floor(q/4). SUPERHEATED return = floor(q/2). The remainder stays in the crucible.

openPoints.point: Which quantities temperature is judged on
openPoints.assumption: The quantities after overflow in the same cycle. States are not re-judged after the bleed or the tap; that happens only at the next cycle's temperature step.

openPoints.point: Which states and quantities the bleed uses
openPoints.assumption: The states just set by the temperature step and the quantities before any bleed transfer. All transfers are applied at once, so melt returned into a crucible is not bled again in that cycle.

openPoints.point: Whether the tap test uses the total before or after slag removal
openPoints.assumption: The total of the six crucibles after the bleed. Slag is not counted. Exactly 38 does not fire the tap (as in cycle 3).

Left as they are (e.g. 10 in crucible 2, a working volume of 8). They are corrected at the next cycle's overflow, or stay that way after cycle 5. The tap halving is applied to them like any other crucible.

run.notes: The arithmetic was done with a short Python script fed to python on stdin. I checked cycle 1 by hand and it matched. A file named sim.py that I wrote to the scratchpad was overwritten by another process sharing that directory: it held a different model with GREEN/HOT states and a different tap rounding. A second file I wrote there did not persist. I left the other files alone and ran the script from stdin instead; no other files are relevant.
